events.title: JavaScript ES5 standardized
events.summary: On December 3, 2009, the ES5 standard was adopted — adding strict mode, built-in [JSON] support, and safer object handling to JavaScript.
events.about: ES5 was the first major JavaScript update in ten years. Strict mode (`"use strict"`) caught common bugs; built-in `[JSON].parse` and `[JSON].stringify` replaced third-party libraries; getters and setters enabled cleaner APIs. It was what jQuery-era websites ran on before modern JavaScript (ES6) became mainstream.

narrative.whyChosen: ES5 was the first meaningful JavaScript update in a decade and fixed real inconsistencies between browsers.
narrative.whyImportant: Developers could parse [JSON] natively and write stricter, less buggy code — without waiting years for the bigger ES6 overhaul.
narrative.problemSolved: A failed ES4 rewrite had frozen the language; browsers and developers needed practical improvements they could ship now.
